moments.act: Asleep. Phone charging on the nightstand.
moments.prompt: The phone is not being used, yet it is still producing records. What does 'off' actually mean for a device like this?

entries.count_basis: Roughly one mast handover per hour while stationary overnight
Minute-level heart rate and movement samples across an 8-hour night
Background app refreshes and ad SDK pings from apps not opened since yesterday
One overnight sleep-quality inference

moments.act: Alarm. First unlock of the day.
moments.prompt: A single unlock produces a wake-consistency inference. Who benefits from knowing a person's chronotype, and how?

entries.count_basis: Alarm dismissal, unlock, and the first two app opens
Night's sleep summary uploaded as a single record
One chronotype/wake-consistency inference

moments.prompt: The electricity meter can tell a shower from a kettle. What else could a fine-grained appliance signal reveal about a household?

entries.count_basis: Two disaggregated appliance events: shower, then kettle
One occupancy/routine inference for the morning window

moments.act: Reads the news on the sofa.
moments.prompt: Reading the news broadcasts a profile of the reader to a market of bidders before the page even finishes loading. Does the reader have any practical way to know who received it?

entries.count_basis: Six page loads while reading the news
A fraction of the ICCL-estimated real-time-bidding broadcasts spread across a day of browsing
One political-leaning inference drawn from the articles read

moments.prompt: Two neighbours' doorbell cameras record this moment without their owner's involvement at all. Whose data is this?

entries.count_basis: Own doorbell plus two neighbours' cameras along the path to the street
Passers-by incidentally recorded in the same frames

moments.prompt: No address was ever typed into any form, yet home and work locations can be inferred from where a routine journey begins and ends. Is that different from being told directly?

entries.count_basis: One tap at boarding
Onboard camera plus one platform camera
Mast handovers along a twenty-minute route
One home/work-address inference from where the journey begins and ends

moments.prompt: One coffee generates a bank record, a retailer record, and a wifi sighting. Which of these would the buyer expect, and which would surprise them?

entries.count_basis: One card transaction
One itemised receipt line
One wifi probe captured at the counter
One update to the daily-spend-rhythm model

moments.act: At a desk until half twelve.
moments.prompt: A flight-risk score can be computed before an employee has decided anything. What would change if employees could see their own score?

entries.count_basis: Badge swipes between zones over the morning
Keystroke-rate and idle-time samples taken every thirty seconds across 3.4 hours
One meeting transcript
One productivity/flight-risk score update
Five colleagues transcribed in the same meeting

moments.prompt: Forty strangers are captured in frame on a five-minute walk. None of them chose to be part of this record. Whose consent, if anyone's, applies here?

entries.count_basis: One incidental plate read passing a junction camera
High-street cameras along the route
Location-linked bid requests from apps running in the foreground
Strangers incidentally captured along the route

moments.prompt: A search typed in privacy becomes a sensitive-category inference attached to an advertising profile. What is the gap between how private this feels and how private it is?

entries.count_basis: Four search queries with timestamp and location
Trackers embedded on the health pages read
One health-condition inference attached to the profile

moments.act: Texts back and forth. Calls mum.
moments.prompt: A closeness ranking of relationships is built from metadata alone, with no message ever read. Is metadata-only analysis less revealing than reading content, or just differently revealing?

entries.count_basis: Call and message metadata across the exchange
One relationship-closeness update
This number, as held in someone else's synced contacts

moments.prompt: This is the same journey as the morning, generating the same kinds of record. Does repetition make a record more or less significant?

entries.count_basis: One tap at boarding
Onboard camera and barrier camera
Mast handovers along the route

moments.act: Big shop on the way back.
moments.prompt: Items bought as gifts are filed as the account holder's own habits. What happens to accuracy when a single account has to represent an entire household?

entries.count_basis: Every item in the basket, linked by the loyalty card
Store cameras and shelf sensors along the aisles
One basket-composition inference
Three items bought for other people, filed as this account's own habit

moments.act: Two hours in front of the television.
moments.prompt: Automatic content recognition samples the screen many times a minute, including from other devices plugged into the TV. Where is the boundary of 'the television' as a data-collecting object?

entries.count_basis: Screen samples taken every fifteen seconds across two hours, including from a plugged-in console
Pauses, rewinds, and one programme abandoned after four minutes
One household-composition inference from co-viewing

moments.prompt: The feed shown here is shaped by what similar late-night users stayed on — people this person has never met. What does it mean to be shown something curated by strangers' compulsions?

entries.count_basis: Dwell time, scroll velocity, hovers, and rewatches across the session
Three messages typed and then deleted before sending
Further bid requests, now carrying a night-time signal
One updated mood-volatility score
One feed re-ranked using similar late-night users' behaviour

moments.act: Asleep. The wearable picks back up.
moments.prompt: Tomorrow's readiness score is computed before tomorrow has happened. Looking back across the whole day: which single record, if any, feels most consequential — and is it one of the roughly twenty inferences, or one of the thousands of emissions?

entries.count_basis: Heart rate resumed at minute intervals
One readiness-score update, already computed for tomorrow
